title: Cycle capacity opportunity mapping and decision calendar
creator: Priya Malhotra
description:
Problem: Every cycle we under- or over-commit because decisions about scope cuts and staffing occur ad hoc during the last week. This creates reactive firefighting, uneven feature quality, and hidden OTE risk.

Goal: Build a repeatable 'opportunity map + decision calendar' that makes capacity-visible decisions early (T-3 to T-2 weeks before engineering freeze). Deliverables: a scoring model for candidate scope items (impact, cost, risk, infra weight), a decision calendar with staffed decision owners and fallback options, and a set of communication artifacts (Linear views, one-pager for exec sign-off, and a dashboard tile in Console showing expected token cost delta).

Approach:
1) Ingest last three cycles' scope vs. actuals from Cycle Analytics and Runtime cost reports.
2) Define a concise 6-factor scoring rubric (user impact, revenue alignment, infra cost per 1k tokens, implementation complexity, cross-team dependencies, regression risk).
3) Triage candidate scope into: Keep, Defer, Minimally Viable, or Defer-with-guardrails.
4) Publish a public decision calendar (weekly slots during T-3/T-2) where owners present a 5-slide ask and a precomputed score.
5) Automate a Linear label + sort view that surfaces top 10 items likely to change decision.

Why different: Focuses on treatable "capacity opportunities" (where small scope changes yield large throughput/cost/latency gains) rather than only prioritizing feature value. This will reduce token cost overruns and reduce last-minute triage load on eng leads.
acceptance_criteria: Scoring rubric documented and validated with Eng + Data + PM (signoff by cycle lead)
Decision calendar template created and published to Confluence + shared with execs
Linear saved view created that auto-labels candidate scope items and ranks by score
Dashboard widget (Console) showing projected per-cycle token cost delta for accepted vs deferred items
At least one mid-cycle decision executed using the new calendar and recorded outcomes (postmortem)

notes: Trade-off: A heavier scoring model reduces ambiguity but increases prep time; we biased toward lighter scoring to keep meeting cycles efficient.
We will surface two types of capacity opportunities: quick wins (<=2 dev days) and systemic items (infra and batching changes) which require a dedicated follow-up plan.
If ENG-22567 is delayed, use historical per-model token runtime as a proxy for infra weight. Plan to re-score items when telemetry is available.
Communication: Decision outcomes must be recorded as comments on each Linear issue and referenced in weekly sync notes so rollout teams can act immediately.
